limitations: Screening result on unvalidated, uncalibrated models; no plant validation is claimed.
The score is an ordinal evidence tally (supports 3/2/1 minus contradictions 6/2/1 for strong/moderate/weak), not a probability and not a certified cause.
The chatter model is linear: it cannot predict limit-cycle amplitude, mark severity or strip break, and a forced response at an unstable operating point is formal only.
Strip spans are lumped springs (inaccurate near the span wave resonance c/(2L)).
Circular (Hitchcock) roll flattening is not valid toward foil gauges; thinner passes need supplied bite sensitivities (model_options.bite_response_override).
The bite-damping closure (fraction beta of transit time) is a declared heuristic; results without it (beta = 0) are reported alongside.
Friction is an input unless tribology.use_computed_friction is set; the friction-speed closure of bite_tribology is an unfitted placeholder whose slope, not level, is used.
Fifth-octave regeneration (backup-roll marking) is screened kinematically, not simulated in time; the antisymmetric mode frequency is an undamped lumped estimate.
Spray coverage is a geometric footprint count; the phase-1 thermal growth is a free-expansion upper bound with no axial conduction (the v2 width_model solves the roll temperature field instead).
The lengthwise physics (roll thermal stripes, shape chain, coil ridges, troughs) rests on planner-derived and memory formulas flagged in each result; no plant validation.

herringbone.threshold_basis: Reduction band 0.40-0.45 from Szucs et al. 2020 / Alcoa citing Schey (hard Al-Mg); the split into ELEVATED/HIGH and the 0.5-2 pitch band are analyst choices.

limitations: Rule-based screen for Type A (yield-point) Luders lines only; Type B (serrated-flow) lines in Al-Mg are not covered.
Ageing, strain rate and temperature effects are not modelled.
reasons: Temper H19 is strain hardened; cold work of about 1-2 % removes the yield plateau.
sources: Choi, Jin, Kang (1998) Scripta Mater. 38(6):887 (Type A Luders below ~40 um grain size)
Reynolds US 4,081,294 (1978) (>= 2 % cold reduction suppresses Type A; 5182-O yield ~139 MPa)

luders_susceptibility.threshold_basis: Mg >= 2 wt% and 1 % cold-work limits are analyst choices within the cited ranges (Reynolds: >= 2 %; Li et al.: 1 % pre-stretch); 40 um grain limit from Choi, Jin & Kang 1998.

limitations: Ignores entry/exit bending at deflector rolls and coilers, which is screened separately by yield_point_bending_window.
reasons: Pass thickness strain 0.3567 (reduction 0.300 > 0.02) exceeds the Luders strain 0.0000: the bite strains the whole strip through the plateau, and the cold work suppresses later yield-point marks. Only skin passes, levelling or bending can leave Luders bands.
sources: Reynolds US 4,081,294 (1978) (>= 2 % cold reduction suppresses Type A; 5182-O yield ~139 MPa)

pass_reduction_vs_luders.threshold_basis: 2 % reduction from Reynolds US 4,081,294; comparison of strains is an analyst rule.

limitations: Geometric footprint count only: no flow-rate distribution across the fan, no heat-transfer coefficient, no drift or deflection.
Positions are barrel coordinates; map strip edges onto the barrel before comparing with observed bands.
reasons: 32 of 32 nozzles active; effective footprint 0.0915 m vs pitch 0.0520 m (overlap fraction 0.431).
Under-cooled stripes give a local thermal crown and differential oil plate-out, which can print a lengthwise band at that width position.
Coverage alternates between overlap and single-fan zones at the nozzle pitch even with no blocked nozzle (cause NOZZLE_PATTERN).
sources: Lloyd (Lechler, 2010) "Fundamentals of roll cooling and control of flatness at primary cold reduction"
Tucker (Lechler, 2006) "Flatness and profile ... spray actuators"
spray_coverage.threshold_basis: Under-coverage is defined relative to the length-weighted modal coverage count (analyst choice); stripe cause labels are geometric (blocked-nozzle footprint overlap, barrel edge, else nozzle pattern).

limitations: Free expansion with no axial heat conduction overestimates the growth of a narrow hot stripe, possibly by a large factor.
Strip lateral constraint converts most of a local gap difference into elongation (flatness) rather than a thickness band.
reasons: Free-expansion radius growth 1.200e-05 m closes the local gap by 1.143e-01 of the exit gauge.
The same roll growth is a larger fraction of thinner strip, so spray stripes matter more as gauge thins.
sources: Lloyd (Lechler, 2010) "Fundamentals of roll cooling and control of flatness at primary cold reduction"
Tucker (Lechler, 2006) "Flatness and profile ... spray actuators"
thermal.threshold_basis: ANALYST_CHOICE (1e-3); even smaller local gap differences can show as flatness defects.

source_disagreements: Effect of friction on chatter is disputed: Yarita (high friction worse), Chefneux (low friction worse), Kimura et al. 2003 (an optimum band). This model gives whatever its slab-derived sensitivities give; see the lever table.
Effect of tension is disputed: Heidari (little effect) vs Zeng, Zang & Gao 2016 (higher tension lowers the critical speed).
The lumped-spring strip span is inaccurate near the span axial wave resonance c/(2L) (about 640 Hz for a 4 m aluminium span); Niroomand et al. 2015 compare lumped and wave span models.
